title: src/wasm/ (12 files) is reachable from no addTest root and re-exported by neither bpm.zig nor main.zig
notes: Incidental finding #3 of the WF-03 Step 1 diagnosis for GH #439 / ISS-0137 (docs/issue-reports/ISS-0137-diagnosis.yaml). Broader than #439: the whole src/wasm subsystem is unreferenced, not merely its tests. Only tests/unit/wasm_executor_test.zig appears in #439's 55-file list (cluster C5); wiring that one test does not answer whether src/wasm is live, prototype, or dead code. src/wasm/wasmtime_bindings.zig may need a real Wasmtime link, which determines whether the test can run in CI at all.
candidate_resolution: Decide liveness of src/wasm. If live: re-export via src/bpm.zig and add an addTest root. If prototype/dead: delete, or record a documented exclusion. Document the wasmtime external-link requirement either way.
resolution:
VERDICT: LIVE. src/wasm is production code backed by 14 requirements (WASM-01..14, 11 MUST + 2 SHOULD), every one RELEASED, and every one of the 12 files appears in some requirement implemented_in list in docs/requirements.yaml. Not deleted.

WIRED: build.zig now passes the wasm named module into bpm_src_mod, and src/bpm.zig re-exports pub const wasm = @import("wasm"). The import is BY NAME, never a relative path: every src/wasm/*.zig reaches its siblings relatively (engine.zig -> wasmtime_bindings.zig, executor.zig -> five siblings, ...), so those files are already owned by wasm_mod; @import("wasm/mod.zig") would enrol them into a second module and Zig 0.16 rejects with 'file exists in multiple modules' (the Single-Owner Module Rule already documented for src/repository and src/oidc).

MADE SELF-ENFORCING: src/wasm carries ZERO in-file test blocks across all 19 files, so it was never test-bearing and lint_test_wiring.py never flagged it -- and a bare re-export would still not be checked, because Zig only semantically analyses decls that something actually references. Added tests/unit/wasm_reexport_test.zig (aggregated into tests/unit/bpm_src_test_root.zig) which touches a concrete decl from every file in the subsystem, so a compile break anywhere under src/wasm/ now fails zig build test.

ROT FOUND AND FIXED BY THAT TEST: the first run failed on src/wasm/wasmtime_bindings.zig:70 callconv(.C) -- valid when written (Stage 9, May 2026) but Zig 0.16 turned CallingConvention into a tagged union whose C member is lowercase .c. Corrected. This is direct proof of the harm the issue described: the subsystem had been silently uncompilable and no target went red.

EXTERNAL-LINK QUESTION (the open half of the issue): NO LINK IS NEEDED, confirmed independently. src/wasm contains zero @cImport and zero linkSystemLibrary. wasmtime_bindings.zig declares only extern struct/extern union TYPES -- extern there is a memory-layout qualifier, not a link-time symbol reference -- and every binding fn is an inline fn stub returning a failure sentinel (engine_new -> null, module_new -> 1). That file's own header says real @cImport bindings arrive in Stage 10. Linking Wasmtime is a Stage 10 concern, not a prerequisite for compiling the subsystem today. Documented in src/bpm.zig, in build.zig, and in the new test file header comment.

tests/unit/wasm_executor_test.zig was left wired exactly as GH #439 left it -- not un-wired, not deleted.

VERIFIED: python tools/lint_test_wiring.py exit 0 (253 test-bearing files, up from 252); zig build exit 0; zig build test exit 0.
prevention: A subsystem with zero in-file test blocks is invisible to tools/lint_test_wiring.py, which only tracks test-bearing files. Build-graph reachability and test reachability are different properties and the existing gate only measures the second. Two habits close the gap: (1) when a subsystem is re-exported purely for reachability, add a test that references a concrete decl from each of its files -- a bare pub const x = @import(...) is never analysed by Zig and so silently rots; (2) when marking requirements RELEASED, confirm the files listed in implemented_in are reachable from some build target, otherwise RELEASED status is not backed by anything that compiles. Consider extending lint_test_wiring.py (or a sibling linter) to flag any src/ directory that no module root and no addTest root reaches, regardless of whether it contains test blocks -- that check would have caught both this issue and ISS-0153 (src/lua) automatically.
